findings.description: none: Ordinary issue create/update cannot attach the reserved marker and ordinary update/close cannot mutate a registry-owned row. `_reject_reserved_projection_label` runs before any DB call in `IssueService.create` (issue_service.py:274) and `IssueService.update` (issue_service.py:425); update and close both go through `mutate_issue_if_unowned`, which takes `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the issue row (039:426-428), refuses owned UUIDs (432-437) and existing/patched reserved labels (438-446) before its single UPDATE (448-462). All four HTTP entry points (`POST /issues/create` 1355, `/issues/update` 1446, `/issues/close` 1478, `PATCH /issues/{id}/labels` 3272) map `ProjectionIssueMutationError` to HTTP 403. Each batched close is its own row-locked RPC call, so per-row check/write races are closed for every allowlisted field. No other `work_queue` write path exists in `src/` outside the projection and claim/complete RPCs.

none: Both projection RPCs insert with `labels=ARRAY[]` (submit 151-159, reconcile 297-304), register the UUID in `work_queue_projection_ownership` (177-178, 322-323) and only then apply the exact canonical pair (193, 374), all inside the function transaction under the per-change advisory lock (97, 248). `enforce_projection_label_ownership` (398-417) fires `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF labels` and rejects the marker on any unowned row; because ownership is an FK to `work_queue(id)`, no insert can be pre-owned, so all post-migration unowned inserts and label updates fail with `42501`. Explicit administrator adoption of a pre-039 row is exercised in `test_039_upgrade_fails_closed_until_owner_registers_verified_row` (test_fresh_database_migration.py:281-299) and unlocks newer-generation repair.

none: The service layer, not only the HTTP route, evaluates `publish_work_projection` with `resource=<change_id>` and audit context `{mode: submit|reconcile, change_id}` whenever a projection key is present (work_queue.py:777-800 submit, 922-933 reconcile). Direct MCP `submit_work`/`reconcile_work_projection` (coordination_mcp.py:377-386, 419-428) call these service methods with no separate `submit_work` check, so no in-process caller can publish a keyed projection under the ordinary operation. `publish_work_projection` is in `ADMIN_ACTIONS` (policy_engine.py:74), trust-3 `TRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS` (agents_config.py:1051), the Cedar schema/policy, and migration 039 profile backfill (10-32). `test_standard_trust_cannot_publish_projection` pins the HTTP 403.

none: `CedarPolicyEngine._check_operation_impl` now reads `ctx.get("trust_level")` and, when omitted, calls the shared `resolve_trust_level`; `TrustResolutionError` becomes a logged `PolicyDecision.deny("trust_resolution_failed: ...")` returned before policy load or Cedar evaluation (735-752), mirroring the native engine (180-210). Denials surface as `failure_category="policy"` in both `submit` and `reconcile_projection` before the RPC, and the guardrail block re-raises `TrustResolutionError` instead of swallowing it (work_queue.py:880-885, 972-973).

none: In-process `converge()` resolves the vendor panel with `_orchestrator_for_dispatch(None, worktree_path)` (convergence_loop.py:615) using the reviewed `worktree_path: Path` parameter (560-564). The resolver honours explicit `agents_yaml`, then the reviewed checkout's local `agents.yaml`, then the coordinator, then global disk (review_dispatcher.py:2575-2591), and only falls back past the coordinator when both `adapters` and `sdk_adapters` are empty (2588), so SDK-only coordinator rosters remain authoritative.

none: Mode isolation runs before the head `FOR UPDATE` read and before any row mutation in both RPCs: any unowned reserved-labelled row for the change returns `projection_key_collision` in either mode (98-112, 249-263); labelled requests against any complete unowned keyed row return `projection_key_collision` (113-127, 264-278); unlabelled requests against any owned row return `projection_mode_mismatch` (128-135, 279-286). Exact-key replay of an owned row dedups via `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and re-applies the label pair (160-193); newer-generation labelled reconcile cancels only owned active rows and clears their labels (344-362); unlabelled reconcile keeps its historical tuple cancellation (332-342) only when no owned or reserved-labelled state exists; head is upserted only after all preflights (326-329). Pre-039 upgrade is pinned by the fresh-migration upgrade tests (test_fresh_database_migration.py:235-345).

none: Direct MCP `submit_work` and `reconcile_work_projection` accept `projection_labels` and forward it on both the local-service and HTTP-proxy branches (coordination_mcp.py:331, 367, 385, 408, 419, 428); `proxy_submit_work`/`proxy_reconcile_work_projection` include the pair in the JSON body only when supplied (http_proxy.py:481, 501-502, 513, 529-530), and the bridge validates and forwards it the same way (coordination_bridge.py:698-703, 758-763, 794-798). `_PROJECTION_CONFLICTS` now contains `projection_mode_mismatch` and `projection_key_collision`, so every RPC conflict reason is returned as an RFC 7807 HTTP 409 (coordination_api.py:95-101, 126-127, 854-873) rather than a trigger exception; `test_projection_key_collision_maps_to_conflict` and `test_projection_conflict_returns_409_problem` pin this.

none: `PATCH /issues/{issue_id}/labels` wraps `IssueService.update(labels=...)` in `except ProjectionIssueMutationError` and raises HTTP 403 with the structured reason (3267-3273). For an owned row the service-level reserved-label guard fires before any RPC (the current labels carry the marker), and for a removal-only patch the RPC returns `projection_issue_immutable` after locking the row and before its UPDATE, so the row is preserved in both cases. `test_patch_issue_labels_maps_projection_refusal_to_forbidden` is parametrised over both `projection_issue_immutable` and `reserved_projection_label` and asserts status 403 and `detail == reason` (test_kanban_viz_endpoints.py:490-519).

none: `mutate_issue_if_unowned` checks the locked row's existing labels for the reserved marker (438-440) and the patch's labels (441-446) and returns structured `reserved_projection_label` before the UPDATE statement at 448, so the `UPDATE OF labels` ownership trigger is never reached for an unowned pre-registry reserved row. `test_039_issue_mutation_fails_closed_on_reserved_upgrade_row` applies a non-label `{"status": "completed"}` patch to the pre-039 spoof row and asserts the structured reason plus unchanged `status='pending'` and labels (test_fresh_database_migration.py:347-369).

none: On the owned labelled path the canonical row is inserted with empty labels, so `notify_projection_insert` (039:468-498, AFTER INSERT, gated on the marker) never fires and cannot fire for any post-039 insert because the BEFORE INSERT ownership trigger rejects marked inserts. First-generation visibility comes from `UPDATE work_queue SET labels=p_projection_labels` (039:193, 374), which trips `notify_work_queue_change` on `OLD.labels IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.labels` with the marker in NEW (037:75-110) and emits change-scoped `projection.labels_changed`; `event_stream.py` collapses that into a `snapshot` (270-279, 320-328). Reactivation adds an explicit notify (039:203-209). design.md:27, change-context.md D5, tasks.md 2.7 and the operator guide all attribute the first event to the migration-037 UPDATE and state the insert trigger is not relied upon; behaviour and documentation agree.

none: The Kanban OpenAPI document now declares `"403": Projection-owned or reserved-label issue mutation is forbidden` on `PATCH /issues/{issue_id}/labels` (kanban-viz.yaml:116), and `test_kanban_label_patch_openapi_declares_projection_forbidden` parses the YAML and asserts the 403 response exists with a projection-referencing description (test_autopilot_projection_visibility.py:220-231), so the contract and runtime are pinned together.

none: Upgrade guidance is consistent across the migration `COMMENT ON TABLE` (039:37-41: adopt every verified keyed row for the change), design.md:74 (inserts every verified complete keyed row UUID for that change), and the operator guide (enumerate every complete keyed row; cancelled historical generations remain part of the fail-closed set; adopting only the current row is insufficient). This matches the SQL: the labelled preflight at 039:113-127 rejects any complete unowned keyed row regardless of status or labels, so a cancelled 038-era generation with cleared labels still blocks until adopted.

Stale migration attribution in the operator guide: "Migration 038 applies canonical labels and clears stale owned labels inside the same per-change transaction that advances or repairs the projection head." At HEAD migration 039 drops and redefines both RPCs (039:43-44, 217-218); 038's versions inserted labelled rows directly and had no ownership registry, which is exactly the behaviour 039 replaced. The same file's later paragraphs correctly credit 039, so the sentence is internally inconsistent and could send an operator to the wrong migration when reasoning about label staging.

Direct-transport MCP `issue_update` and `issue_close` do not handle `ProjectionIssueMutationError`; it falls into the blanket `except Exception` (716-720, 768-772), which logs a full stack trace at ERROR via `logger.exception` and returns `reason: "ProjectionIssueMutationError: projection_issue_immutable"`. The refusal is still enforced (the RPC never mutates), but an expected policy refusal is reported as an internal failure and the structured reason is prefixed, unlike the HTTP 403 and the proxy transport's `{"error": "http_403", "detail": {...}}` envelope.
findings.resolution: Add `except ProjectionIssueMutationError as e: return {"success": False, "reason": str(e)}` before the generic handler in `issue_update`, `issue_close`, and `issue_create`.

findings.description: Behavioural narrowing not called out in the change artifacts: `mutate_issue_if_unowned` selects `WHERE id=p_issue_id AND task_type='issue'` (426-428) and returns `issue_not_found` otherwise. Previously `IssueService.update`/`close` used `db.update("work_queue", match={"id": ...})` with no task-type filter, so a caller passing an ordinary task UUID to `/issues/update`, `/issues/close`, or the MCP `issue_close` tool could mutate it; at HEAD such calls return `None`/HTTP 404 (update) or silently drop the id from the batch result (close). The tighter contract is arguably correct for an issue API, but it is an unannounced compatibility change for operator scripts that closed ordinary tasks through the issue tools.
findings.resolution: Add a one-line note to the operator guide or proposal non-goals.

findings.description: Coverage gap, not an observed defect: no live PostgreSQL test drives `IssueService.update`/`close` through `mutate_issue_if_unowned` and back through `_issue_from_mutation_result` and `Issue.from_row` on the `to_jsonb(v_issue)` payload. The RPC is exercised only via raw SQL in `test_fresh_database_migration.py` and the service only against `AsyncMock` rows. Static reading shows the round-trip should work (jsonb renders timestamptz as ISO-8601 with `+00:00`, which `datetime.fromisoformat` accepts; UUIDs and arrays become strings/lists), but a successful mutation path with real column types is unpinned.
findings.resolution: Add an `IssueService` update+close assertion against the live database in `test_autopilot_projection_acceptance_postgres.py`.

findings.description: `try_projection_issue_list` and `try_projection_issue_update` have no production caller (only tests reference them, and the adapter tests assert they are never invoked). `try_projection_issue_update` posts to `/issues/update` with a `labels` patch, which at HEAD is refused with HTTP 403 for every registry-owned row, so the helper can no longer do what its docstring says. Dead code that documents a now-forbidden path is a trap for a future caller.
findings.resolution: Remove both helpers or mark them deprecated with a pointer to the projection RPCs.

findings.description: Re-confirmed round-15 observation, unchanged at HEAD: `IssueService.close` issues one `mutate_issue_if_unowned` RPC per id and `_issue_from_mutation_result` raises on the first owned/reserved id, so `POST /issues/close` returns 403 after earlier ids in the batch were already committed and the partial `results` list is discarded (coordination_api.py:1471-1481). Each row is individually race-safe; only the batch envelope leaks side effects. Round 15 accepted this as a separate contract; no regression.
